title: HB 2785 (2024 - Fifty-sixth Legislature - Second Regular Session (azleg session id 128)): primary; identification; canvass; recounts; ballots
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 1: Section 16-411, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 4)
(quote) A voting center shall allow any voter in that county to receive the appropriate ballot for that voter on election day after presenting identification as prescribed in section 16-579 and to lawfully cast the ballot.
(section) Sec. 4: Section 16-542, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Any on-site early voting location or other early voting location shall require each elector to present identification as prescribed in section 16-579 before receiving a ballot.
(section) Sec. 4: Section 16-542, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para E)
(quote) An elector who appears personally not later than 7:00 p.m. on the Friday preceding the election at an on-site early voting location that is established by the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall be given a ballot after presenting identification as prescribed in section 16-579 and shall be allowed to vote at the on-site location.
(section) Sec. 4: Section 16-542, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para H)
(quote) Before voting pursuant to this subsection, an elector who experiences an emergency shall provide identification as prescribed in section 16-579 and shall sign a statement under penalty of perjury that states that the person is experiencing or experienced an emergency after 7:00 p.m. on the Friday immediately preceding the election and before 5:00 p.m. on the Monday immediately preceding the election that would prevent the person from voting at the polls.
(section) Sec. 5: Section 16-547, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) Bringing the ballot to any polling place in the county not later than 7:00 p.m. on election day and choosing to present valid identification that complies with section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 1, Arizona Revised Statutes.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Beginning with the first missing or mismatched signature that is identified after the period of early voting begins through the Monday immediately preceding the election, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall submit daily to the political parties that are qualified for continued REPRESENTATION on the state ballot an updated list of all voters whose signatures are missing or inconsistent with the voter's signature on the voter's registration record.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (a) A valid form of identification that bears the photograph, name and address of the elector that reasonably appear to be the same as the name and address in the precinct register, including an Arizona driver license, an Arizona nonoperating identification license, a tribal enrollment card or other form of tribal identification or a United States federal, state or local government issued identification.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (a) REQUIRE THE VOTER TO PRESENT IDENTIFICATION THAT COMPLIES WITH PARAGRAPH 1 OF THIS SUBSECTION.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (b) CONFIRM THAT THE NAME AND ADDRESS ON THE IDENTIFICATION REASONABLY APPEAR TO BE THE SAME NAME AND ADDRESS SHOWN ON THE VOTER'S REGISTRATION RECORD.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para C)
(quote) The voter shall present a form of identification that includes the voter's given name and surname and the voter's complete residence address.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 5: Section 16-547, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) I declare the following under penalty of perjury: At the registered voter's request I assisted the voter identified in this affidavit with marking the voter's ballot, I marked the ballot as directly instructed by the voter, I provided the assistance because the voter was physically unable to mark the ballot solely due to illness, injury or physical limitation and I understand that there is no power of attorney for voting and that the voter must be able to make the voter's selection even if the voter cannot physically mark the ballot.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) A. Except for early ballots tabulated as prescribed in section 16-579.02 or, beginning in 2026, received at a voting location after a voter's identification is CONFIRMED as prescribed by section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 4, on receipt of the envelope containing the early ballot and the mail ballot affidavit, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall compare the signature on the envelope with the signature of the elector on the elector's registration record as prescribed by section 16-550.01.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Beginning on the Wednesday immediately following the election through the end of the signature cure period after a primary, general or special election that includes a federal office, or the third business day after the election for any other election, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall submit daily to the political parties that are qualified for continued representation on the state ballot an updated list of all voters whose signatures are inconsistent with the voter's signature on the voter's registration record and all voters who voted with a conditional provisional ballot.
(section) Sec. 8: Section 16-551, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para C)
(quote) Beginning in 2026, all early ballots that are delivered by a voter to a voting location without presenting identification that complies with section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 1 must be signature verified.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) A valid form of identification that bears the photograph, name and address of the elector except that if the address on the identification does not reasonably appear to be the same as the address in the precinct register or the identification is a valid United States military identification card or a valid United States passport and does not bear an address, the identification must be accompanied by one of the items listed in subdivision (b) of this paragraph.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 2)
(quote) 2. If the elector does not present identification that complies with paragraph 1 of this subsection, the elector is only eligible to vote a provisional ballot as prescribed by section 16-584 or a conditional provisional ballot as provided for in the secretary of state's instruction and procedures manual adopted pursuant to section 16-452.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 3)
(quote) 3. Through 2025, if the voter surrenders the early ballot to the precinct inspector and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter shall be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to this subsection.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) Stamp the signed affidavit with a stamp that reads "ID verified" and place the stamped affidavit that contains the early ballot in a secured ballot box that is labeled for early ballots.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 1)
(quote) 1. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has not been returned or accepted by the county recorder and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter may be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to subsection A of this section.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 2)
(quote) 2. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has been received or accepted by the county recorder, the voter may not be issued a standard ballot and may only be issued a provisional ballot as prescribed in section 16-584.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para B)
(quote) B. A qualified elector whose name is not on the precinct register, on presentation of identification verifying the identity of the elector that includes the voter's given name and surname and the complete residence address that is verified by the election board to be in the precinct or on signing an affirmation that states that the elector is a registered voter in that jurisdiction and is eligible to vote in that jurisdiction, shall be allowed to vote a provisional ballot.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para C)
(quote) The voter shall be allowed to vote a provisional ballot.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para D)
(quote) D. On completion of the ballot, the election official shall place the ballot in a provisional ballot envelope and shall deposit the envelope in the ballot box.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para D)
(quote) If the voter's name is not signed on the roster and if there is no indication that the voter voted an early ballot, the provisional ballot envelope shall be opened and the ballot shall be counted.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para D)
(quote) If there is information showing the person did vote, the provisional ballot shall remain unopened and shall not be counted.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para D)
(quote) When provisional ballots are confirmed for counting, the county recorder shall use the information supplied on the provisional ballot envelope to correct the address record of the voter.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para E)
(quote) E. When a voter is allowed to vote a provisional ballot, the elector's name shall be entered on a separate signature roster page at the end of the signature roster.
(section) Sec. 11: Section 16-584, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para F)
(quote) F. For any person who votes a provisional ballot, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall provide for a method of notifying the provisional ballot voter at no cost to the voter whether the voter's ballot was verified and counted and, if not counted, the reason for not counting the ballot.

(section) Sec. 1: Section 16-411, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (b) A qualified elector voting at an emergency voting center shall provide identification as prescribed in section 16-579, except that notwithstanding section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 2, for any voting at an emergency voting center, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections may allow a qualified elector to update the elector's voter registration information as provided for in the secretary of state's instructions and procedures manual adopted pursuant to section 16-452.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) A. Except for early ballots tabulated as prescribed in section 16-579.02 or, beginning in 2026, received at a voting location after a voter's identification is CONFIRMED as prescribed by section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 4, on receipt of the envelope containing the early ballot and the mail ballot affidavit, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall compare the signature on the envelope with the signature of the elector on the elector's registration record as prescribed by section 16-550.01.
(section) Sec. 8: Section 16-551, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para C)
(quote) Beginning in 2026, all early ballots that are delivered by a voter to a voting location without presenting identification that complies with section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 1 must be signature verified.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (b) Two different items that contain the name and address of the elector that reasonably appear to be the same as the name and address in the precinct register, including a utility bill, a bank or credit union statement that is dated within ninety days of the date of the election, a valid Arizona vehicle registration, an Arizona vehicle insurance card, an Indian census card, tribal enrollment card or other form of tribal identification, a property tax statement, a recorder's certificate, a voter registration card, a valid United States federal, state or local government issued identification or any mailing that is labeled as "official election material".
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 3)
(quote) 3. Through 2025, if the voter surrenders the early ballot to the precinct inspector and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter shall be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to this subsection.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 4)
(quote) 4. Beginning in 2026, aT ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL:
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) Stamp the signed affidavit with a stamp that reads "ID verified" and place the stamped affidavit that contains the early ballot in a secured ballot box that is labeled for early ballots.
(section) Sec. 10: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 1)
(quote) 1. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has not been returned or accepted by the county recorder and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter may be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to subsection A of this section.
